stories.title: Muse Glimmer from Meta Superintelligence Labs is now available
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Meta has released Muse Glimmer, its first open model from Meta Superintelligence Labs.
Muse Glimmer is a 30B multimodal model available under the permissive Apache 2.0 license.
It is specifically designed for local coding agents and optimized via Ollama's MLX engine with new DFlash and image input support.

stories.title: Apple will limit Mac disk access as AI agents ‘substantially’ increase risk
stories.author: Emma Roth
bullet_points: Apple is introducing new limitations on 'full disk access' for Macs.
The change is a direct response to security risks posed by increasingly capable AI agents.
The update aims to ensure users must intentionally grant this high level of application access.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights a trending model, deepseek-ai/DeepSeek-R1, on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
The model is categorized for text generation and conversational AI tasks.
It utilizes common ML frameworks and formats like transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the trending status of the meta-llama/Llama-3.1-8B-Instruct model on Hugging Face.
The model is categorized under text-generation, indicating its primary function in language tasks.
It is associated with key ML technologies such as transformers and safetensors.

stories.title: 🤗 Trending: meta-llama/Meta-Llama-3-8B
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: The news highlights the Meta-Llama-3-8B model on Hugging Face Benchmarks.
It is categorized under text-generation and utilizes transformers and safetensors.
This indicates active community interest and benchmarking of a significant LLM release.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA Nemotron 3.5 Lightning, a 30B parameter open model, is now accessible via Ollama.
The model is specifically engineered for autonomous agents capable of multi-step tasks and tool calling.
It is designed to run locally on user hardware, emphasizing on-device AI capabilities.

stories.title: Ollama: all aboard open models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama, a platform for running open models, has secured significant funding.
The company raised $88 million from prominent investors including Y Combinator and Benchmark.
Ollama currently serves a large developer base of 8.9 million users.

stories.title: Faster Gemma 4 on MLX with multi-token prediction
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Gemma 4 inference speed is significantly improved within Ollama 0.31.
The performance boost is achieved on Apple Silicon using MLX and Multi-Token Prediction (MTP).
Coding agent performance saw up to 90% speedup when benchmarked with Aider.

stories.title: Ollama's highest performance on Apple Silicon yet with MLX
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has achieved its peak performance on Apple Silicon.
The performance boost is attributed to updates in the MLX engine.
Improvements include faster response times, higher output quality, and reduced memory usage.

stories.title: An OpenAI safety employee has quit and is sounding the alarm
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: An OpenAI safety employee, David Robinson, has resigned from the company.
Robinson previously authored the safety reports accompanying major OpenAI model releases.
He is now publicly raising concerns about the safety and risks associated with OpenAI's technology.

stories.title: Meta open sources code to let you make Muse AI gadgets
stories.author: Jay Peters
bullet_points: Meta has open-sourced the code for its Muse AI agent.
This allows developers to create custom 'Muse gadgets' for various hardware.
Potential applications include E Ink displays for reminders or HDMI sticks for large-screen viewing.

stories.title: Apple changes full-disk access permissions to curb abuse from AI agents
stories.author: Dan Goodin
bullet_points: Apple is modifying full-disk access permissions to mitigate potential misuse by AI agents.
The change addresses concerns regarding unauthorized access to user data by third-party AI tools.
The article highlights a disagreement between Apple and Meta regarding the sufficiency of current regulatory frameworks (like FDA standards) to prevent such abuse.

stories.title: US arrests tech CEO accused of smuggling $300M in Nvidia chips into China
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: A US tech CEO has been arrested for allegedly smuggling $300 million worth of Nvidia chips into China.
The incident highlights ongoing and persistent issues regarding the illicit trade of advanced semiconductor technology.
The story points to continued regulatory and enforcement challenges in controlling high-tech exports to China.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Introduces GALA, a method to enable real-time animation for 3D Gaussian avatars.
Addresses the computational bottleneck of costly neural inference typically required for avatar animation.
Achieves this by approximating complex animations using a linear combination of identity-independent blendshapes.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: KaliBench introduces a fine-grained benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
It addresses a critical gap in current evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level agentic tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
The benchmark incorporates runtime-free verifiable rewards, allowing for rigorous and accurate assessment of command syntax and tool invocation correctness.

stories.title: VISTA: A Visual Harness for Reasoning in an Interactive World
stories.author: Kaiming He
bullet_points: Introduces VISTA, a visual harness designed to unlock reasoning potential in multimodal AI models.
VISTA provides general-purpose multimodal models with long-horizon vision capabilities in interactive environments.
The system features a lossless visual memory, allowing the model to actively retrieve and process past visual observations.

stories.title: One Basis to Animate Them All: Gaussian Blendshape Distillation for Real-Time Avatars
stories.author: Ivan Laptev
bullet_points: Addresses the computational bottleneck of real-time animation for 3D Gaussian avatars, which typically require costly neural inference.
Proposes GALA (Gaussian Animation via Linear Approximation), a distillation method to approximate complex avatar animations.
Replaces per-frame heavy neural decoding with a more efficient, shallow coefficient predictor based on linear combinations of blendshapes.

stories.title: The Missing Primitive: Diagnosing and Repairing Mathematical Reasoning in Large Language Models
stories.author: Zhengzhong Tu
bullet_points: The research addresses the fundamental question of whether LLMs possess true structural mathematical understanding, rather than just pattern matching.
The paper introduces the concept of 'Mathematical Primitive' as a novel method to systematically probe and diagnose LLM capabilities in mathematics.
The findings aim to provide actionable insights for improving LLMs through targeted post-training techniques.

stories.title: Ollama now supports Jev-style decision models
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama has integrated support for Jev-style decision models via TypeSafe's Jev API.
These models enable fast, low-latency, and cost-free decision-making based on text input.
The models provide probabilistic answers to yes/no questions, choices, and scoring.

stories.title: Claude Desktop support with Ollama
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Claude Desktop now supports Ollama as a third-party gateway.
This integration allows users to run open-source models within the Claude Desktop environment.
It bridges proprietary AI platforms with local, open-weights model ecosystems.

stories.title: Improved performance and model support with GGUF
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: Ollama 0.30 release introduces performance improvements and enhanced GGUF model compatibility.
The update leverages llama.cpp to broaden model support across various hardware configurations.
It augments Ollama's MLX engine specifically for better performance on Apple silicon.

stories.title: NVIDIA Nemotron 3 Ultra
stories.author: unknown
bullet_points: NVIDIA is introducing the Nemotron 3 Ultra model.
The model is specifically engineered for high-throughput reasoning tasks.
It is optimized for supporting long-running agent workflows.

stories.title: Capcom is preparing for a ‘future where we create games together with AI’
stories.author: Terrence O’Brien
bullet_points: Capcom is actively exploring the integration of AI into game development, signaling a shift in industry practices.
A programmer presented on the 'REX Project' during the Capcom Open Conference, indicating ongoing engine evolution.
The news suggests a move towards collaborative game creation involving AI, moving beyond mere thematic representation.

stories.title: Netflix is pivoting away from prestige
stories.author: Charles Pulliam-Moore
bullet_points: Netflix is reportedly changing its content strategy, moving away from high-profile, prestige productions.
This shift is evidenced by Netflix ending multiyear production deals with established, critically acclaimed directors.
The move signals a potential strategic pivot in how the streaming giant approaches content creation compared to rivals.

stories.title: OpenAI’s Dot agent is enterprise software that can also order your dinner
stories.author: Allison Johnson
bullet_points: OpenAI has introduced a new agent platform named 'Dots'.
The platform is positioned as enterprise software, capable of performing tasks like ordering food.
The article contrasts Dots with Meta's Muse, noting Dots have a more 'workplace software' feel.

stories.title: Amazon’s $1B plan to combat data center backlash draws more backlash
stories.author: Ashley Belanger
bullet_points: Amazon has a $1 billion initiative aimed at addressing criticism surrounding its data centers.
The company received mixed reactions, being praised for ending Non-Disclosure Agreements (NDAs).
However, Amazon faced further criticism for allegedly minimizing the environmental impact and pollution from its data centers.

stories.title: Lyft settles landmark driver misclassification lawsuit for $272.5M
stories.author: Cyrus Farivar
bullet_points: Lyft has settled a significant lawsuit regarding the misclassification of its drivers.
The settlement amount reached $272.5 million.
The resolution faces criticism from groups claiming drivers are still owed more.

stories.title: Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real: Guided Self-Improvement for Embodied Agents
stories.author: Haozhi Qi
bullet_points: Introduces 'Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real' (RPG), a framework for autonomous improvement of embodied agents.
RPG allows robots to improve execution skills without requiring updates to the underlying model weights.
The framework uses offline datasets to identify capabilities, generates simulation practice tasks, and leverages execution feedback.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability of AI to find inspiring prior research.
The benchmark is built using human-annotated data from researchers who explicitly point to papers that influenced their own work.
Addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to sense relevant, buried ideas within massive scientific archives.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The approach aims to improve topological preservation and reduce generation costs compared to existing token-based methods.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) are proposed as an alternative to autoregressive models for tasks requiring bidirectional reasoning.
Discrete diffusion models suffer from a bottleneck where parallel decoding samples tokens independently, losing statistical dependencies.
CDLMs address this by denoising a shared continuous state, allowing for better modeling of token dependencies during generation.

stories.title: DMAD: Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for Fast Visual Generation
stories.author: Chongyang Ma
bullet_points: DMAD introduces Distribution Matching as Adversarial Distillation for faster visual generation.
It reframes distribution matching as a classification task, learning log-density ratios directly.
The method aims to reduce the memory and computation overhead associated with auxiliary diffusion models.

stories.title: Higher-Order Molecular Grammars for Generative and Foundation Models in Chemistry
stories.author: Tolga Birdal
bullet_points: Introduces Higher-order Grammar Representation (HGR) to address limitations in molecular learning models.
HGR is designed to explicitly encode complex molecular topologies, such as ring systems and recurring motifs, which standard formalisms struggle with.
The framework aims to be computationally efficient while maintaining topology awareness for generative and foundation models in chemistry.

stories.title: Embedding Prediction Helps Image Generation
stories.author: Stella X. Yu
bullet_points: The research proposes using predicted embeddings as a conditioning mechanism in diffusion transformers for image generation.
The core method involves training a Next-Embedding Predictive Autoregression (NEPA) model to forecast sequential continuous embeddings.
This approach leverages the relationship between noisy and clean image embeddings during the denoising process.

stories.title: SILSA: Sliding-Window Slice Latents for Topology-Preserving High-Resolution 3D Generation
stories.author: Ismini Lourentzou
bullet_points: SILSA introduces a new framework for high-resolution 3D generation using compact sliding-window slice latents.
It addresses limitations in current methods (voxel latents/multi-stage pipelines) which fragment surfaces and weaken topological consistency.
The approach aims to improve topological preservation and reduce generation costs compared to existing local token-based methods.

stories.title: TACO: Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse Optimizer for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: TACO introduces a new optimizer designed to reduce the memory overhead associated with full-parameter fine-tuning of Large Language Models (LLMs).
The optimizer achieves sparsity by using a Ternary Absolute-max Column-wise One-sparse approach, addressing memory limitations on modern GPUs.
It aims to improve upon existing methods (like Muon) by maintaining a geometry closer to AdamW to prevent performance degradation during fine-tuning.

stories.title: Cost-augmented Schrödinger bridges on graphs are exactly solvable: a Feynman-Kac tilt replaces learned control
stories.author: Akshay Balsubramani
bullet_points: The research addresses the problem of finding a generalized Schrödinger bridge on graphs that incorporates a state-visitation cost.
A key theoretical finding is that the cost-augmented bridge can be solved exactly by using a Feynman-Kac tilt on the reference process.
This exact solution eliminates the need for complex learning methods, such as temporal-difference penalties, previously used to incorporate the cost.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models (CDLMs) as an alternative to discrete diffusion models.
CDLMs aim to overcome the independent token sampling bottleneck found in discrete diffusion models during parallel decoding.
The core mechanism involves denoising a shared continuous state, which allows for capturing statistical dependencies between tokens.

stories.title: Trust the Direction, Search the Step: Zero-and-First-Order Methods for LLM Fine-Tuning
stories.author: Aritra Dutta
bullet_points: Addresses the critical challenge of step-size selection in large-scale LLM fine-tuning optimization.
Introduces Zero-and-First-Order optimization (ZFO) to decouple direction selection from step-size.
ZFO uses a first-order optimizer for direction and zeroth-order evaluations along a 1D subspace for step-size selection.

stories.title: KaliBench: A Fine-Grained Benchmark for Cybersecurity Tool Use on Kali Linux with Runtime-Free Verifiable Rewards
stories.author: Muzammal Naseer
bullet_points: Introduces KaliBench, a new benchmark specifically designed to evaluate LLMs' ability to generate executable commands for real-world cybersecurity tools on Kali Linux.
Addresses a critical gap in current LLM evaluations, which often focus on knowledge or high-level tasks rather than precise CLI command generation.
Emphasizes the importance of fine-grained, runtime-free verifiable rewards to accurately measure the syntactic correctness required in cybersecurity operations.

stories.title: ScholarCatalyst: A Benchmark for Retrieving Papers That Inspire New Research
stories.author: Chelsea Finn
bullet_points: Introduces ScholarCatalyst, a new benchmark designed to test the ability to retrieve inspiring prior research papers.
Addresses the challenge of AI systems needing to identify relevant, often buried, prior ideas to spark new research.
Uses an automated pipeline to scale author annotations, making the creation of the benchmark feasible.

stories.title: Hierarchical Continuous Diffusion Language Models
stories.author: Alexander Schwing
bullet_points: Introduces Continuous Diffusion Language Models as an alternative to discrete autoregressive models.
Addresses a key limitation of discrete diffusion models: independent token sampling during parallel decoding.
Proposes using a shared continuous state for denoising to maintain statistical dependencies among decoded tokens.

stories.title: AutoCompact: Learning When to Compact Context in Long-Horizon Coding Agents
stories.author: Xin Dong
bullet_points: Introduces AutoCompact, a method to train coding agents to intelligently manage context in long-horizon software engineering tasks.
Addresses the challenge that early exploration in long coding trajectories becomes stale, requiring agents to decide when and how to compact context.
The agent learns the policy for deciding what working state to preserve when performing context compaction.

stories.title: Keyword Harnesses Fail Open: A Cheap Diagnostic Ladder for Tool-Use Claims in Small Language Models
stories.author: Juan S. Santillana
bullet_points: Keyword-matching benchmarks can falsely credit small language models for tool use they do not actually perform.
The paper introduces a 'cheap diagnostic ladder' to provide stricter evaluation for tool-use claims in LLMs.
The study demonstrates false positives using Spanish security language models, comparing a small, code-heavy model against a larger, curriculum-trained one.

stories.title: Finetuning with Sampling: SFT Learns Better Than You Think
stories.author: Yilun Du
bullet_points: The paper investigates alternative methods to improve frontier models beyond standard Supervised Fine-Tuning (SFT) and Reinforcement Learning (RL).
It challenges the conventional view that RL is superior for generalization while SFT suffers from weak generalization and catastrophic forgetting.
The proposed method, 'Finetuning with Sampling,' offers a new approach to leverage off-policy expert data, potentially improving upon current SFT limitations.

stories.title: Argo-Bench: Evaluating Data Agents on Enterprise-Scale Workflows
stories.author: Joseph J Ma
bullet_points: Argo-Bench is a new evaluation framework designed to test data agents on complex, enterprise-scale workflows.
It addresses the limitations of existing text-to-SQL benchmarks, which only test query generation and often have flawed answer keys.
The framework uses public datasets to simulate real-world scenarios requiring reasoning across multiple tables and statistical analysis.

stories.title: Where-OPD: Spatially Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation of MLLMs with Synthetic Scenes
stories.author: Spyros Gidaris
bullet_points: The paper introduces Where-OPD, a method applying on-policy self-distillation to Multimodal Large Language Models (MLLMs).
This technique aims to improve MLLM reasoning by using a privileged, self-generated supervisory signal.
It addresses a gap in current research where existing MLLM visual guidance methods are often limited in scope.

stories.title: Kolibri: A Sovereign Open-Weight Model
stories.author: bastitx
bullet_points: Introduction of Kolibri, described as a sovereign open-weight model.
The model's focus suggests a push towards decentralized or self-governed AI solutions.
The announcement originates from a technical blog, indicating a deep dive into the model's architecture or philosophy.

stories.title: Show HN: Pi pod – Run your pi coding agent in sandboxes on your own server
stories.author: edverma2
bullet_points: Pi pod allows users to run a 'pi coding agent' in isolated, composable sandboxes on their own servers.
The tool addresses frustration with current AI agent environments, which are often locked into single providers or rely on per-token costs.
It aims to provide a more agnostic and controllable environment for 'agentic engineering' workflows.

stories.title: Pop!_OS bans AI-generated code from much of its codebase
stories.author: bundie
bullet_points: Pop!_OS is implementing a policy to restrict AI-generated code within its software codebase.
This move signals a growing concern or preference within the Linux/open-source community regarding AI code quality and integrity.
The decision represents a notable stance by a major Linux distribution against unchecked reliance on generative AI tools.

stories.title: gVisor is being donated to CNCF
stories.author: gvisor.dev via carlana
bullet_points: gVisor, a container sandbox technology, is being donated to the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF).
This move signifies the project's integration into the broader cloud-native ecosystem.
The donation suggests increased industry adoption and standardization for container security.

stories.title: The Four Horsemen of Agentic Coding
stories.author: distantprovince.substack.com via guillego
bullet_points: The article discusses 'Agentic Coding,' a growing trend in AI development.
It frames the key components or challenges of this paradigm as 'The Four Horsemen.'
The topic suggests a discussion on the evolution and complexity of autonomous coding agents.

stories.title: Auditing 50 Petabytes of Agent Logs Costs More Than Sandboxing Egress
stories.author: reidmarlow
bullet_points: OpenAI has released findings regarding agent intrusions within external infrastructure.
The analysis highlights the significant cost disparity between auditing massive log volumes (50 Petabytes) and sandboxing egress.
This suggests operational and financial challenges associated with monitoring advanced AI agent behavior.
